{{Nihongo|'''Takashi Inoue'''|井之上 喬|Inoue Takashi|born 20 November 1944}} is a [[public relations]] practitioner, scholar, and theorist. His theories include the "[[Hyper-globalization#Three forces of hyper-globalization|three forces of hyper-globalization]]", the "Self-Correction Model of Public Relations",<ref name=":4">{{Cite book|title=The global public relations handbook : theory, research, and practice|last=Inoue|first=Takashi|date=2003|publisher=Lawrence Erlbaum|others=Sriramesh, Krishnamurthy., Verčič, Dejan.|isbn=1410607755|location=Mahwah, N.J.|pages=Introduction pages xxx-xxxi; "An Overview of Public Relations in Japan and the Self-Correction Concept" pages 68–85|oclc=53010962}}</ref> and the "Japan model".<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ipra.org/news/itle/the-japan-model/|title=IPRA {{!}} The Japan Model|website=www.ipra.org|access-date=2019-03-05}}</ref> He was the first to teach public relations courses at a major university in post-war Japan and is the Chairman and CEO of Inoue Public Relations,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.inoue-pr.com/eng/about_us/|title=About Us {{!}} Multidiscipline PR Consultancy Inoue Public Relations, Inc.|website=www.inoue-pr.com|access-date=2019-02-26}}</ref> which he founded in 1970. He is a visiting professor at the Graduate School of Management, Kyoto University<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gsm.kyoto-u.ac.jp/en/about-the-gsm/faculty-information/endowed-chair-class/721-inoue-2.html|title=Takashi INOUE Visiting Professor -Kyoto University, Graduate School of Management, 京都大学経営管理大学院|website=www.gsm.kyoto-u.ac.jp|access-date=2019-02-26}}</ref> and at Kobe Institute of Computing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kic.ac.jp/eng/subject-overview-core-lecture.html|title=Core Subjects (Lectures)|last=Inoue|first=Takashi|website=Kobe Institute of Computing (KIC)|access-date=March 12, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.inoue-pr.com/eng/about_us/|title=Bio of Takashi Inoue|last=Inoue|first=Takashi|date=March 14, 2019}}</ref> He was quoted in foreign press reports on the East Japan Earthquake<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/04/09/world/asia/09nuclear.html |title=Lack of Data Heightens Japan's Nuclear Crisis |author1=Hiroko Tabuchi |author-link=Hiroko Tabuchi |author2=Keith Bradsher |work=The New York Times|date=9 April 2011 |access-date=12 March 2019}}</ref> and the 2018 arrest in Japan of Nissan chairman Carlos Ghosn.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/11/21/business/carlos-ghosn-nissan-detained-10-days.html|title=Nissan's Ghosn to Spend at Least 10 More Days in Custody|last=Motoko Rich and Liz Alderman|date=21 November 2018|work=The New York Times|access-date=12 March 2019}}</ref> He has written about modern Japan's lack of PR skills and has described the resulting "Deficiency of Japanese diplomacy",<ref name=":4" /> and in 2010 he wrote that corporate Japan's scandals have created "A culture of apologies: Communicating crises in Japan"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://apps.prsa.org/Intelligence/TheStrategist/Articles/view/8644/102/A_culture_of_apologies_Communicating_crises_in_Jap|title=A culture of apologies: Communicating crises in Japan|website=PRSA|language=en|access-date=2019-03-25}}</ref>

== Early life ==
He was born in the Chinese city of [[Dalian]] (formerly Dairen, Manshū) at the end of World War II as the sixth child of Rikichi Inoue, who was then the Japanese wartime vice mayor of the city, and Junko Inoue. He first touched Japanese soil before reaching age 2, when the family repatriated after the war. He grew up in Japan as part of the first postwar generation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://bb-relife.jp/interview/ad-communication/1827|title=井之上パブリックリレーションズ/井之上喬 インタビュー「常日頃から準備」|date=2010-10-26|website=起業家インタビューのthe Entrepreneur(アントレプレナー)|language=ja|access-date=2019-03-05}}</ref>

== Theories ==
* '''Self-Correction Model of Public Relations''': To consistently achieve goals and to survive a crisis organizations need to establish a process of two-way communications, ethics, continuous self-correction, and recognition of the central role played by human free-will.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite news|url=http://apps.prsa.org/Intelligence/Tactics/Articles/view/6C-080916/101/Profiles_in_PR_Kizuna_perspectives_Takashi_Inoue_s#.XIr8hygzbIU|title="Kizuna" perspectives: Takashi Inoue's 35 years of PR innovation in Japan|last=Elsasser|first=John|newspaper=Prsa|date=August 2009}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Inoue|first=Takashi|date=October 2009|title=The Self-Correction Model in Public Relations|journal=Frontline Online}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Inoue|first=Takashi|date=October 2002|title=米国におけるパブリック・リレーションズの発展の分析・考察と新しいモデルの提案 [U. S. Public Relations in Transition : Analysis of its Evolution and Proposal for a New Model]|journal=Journal of the Japan Information-culture Society|volume=9(1), 2002-10-20|pages=61–75}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Inoue|first=Takashi|date=2002|title=The Need for Two-Way Communications and Self-Correction|journal=IPRA, Frontline}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite book|title=Public relations in hyper-globalization : essential relationship management : a Japan perspective|last=Inoue|first=Takashi|publisher=Routledge|year=2018|isbn=9781351679626|location=Abingdon, Oxon|pages=Hyper-globalization 11–13; Self-Correction 241–263; PR Life-cycle Model 177–184; Tenneco Report 186–194|oclc=1031676608}}</ref>
* '''Kizuna Education''': "Kizuna", the Japanese word for building relationships between people, is a fundamental skill that helps people live harmoniously in society and to achieve their personal goals through cooperation with others. "Kizuna education" is the concept that it is necessary in today's global society to teach children at very early stages,<ref name=":7">{{Cite web|url=http://kizuna-ehon.com/|title=Kizuna Picture Book Series|last=Kizuna Education}}</ref> including preschool, the skill of relationship building in order to foster global peace.<ref name=":6" />
* '''Public Relations Life-Cycle Model''': Structured public relations process aimed at achieving goals quickly and economically through "win-win" outcomes for both the organization and its many stakeholders. The model includes defining PR objectives, setting communication channels, PR strategy, PR program, implementation, analysis, and correction.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.inoue-pr.com/eng/perspectives/what-pr-means-to-us/|title=What the PR Life-Cycle Model Means}}</ref>
* '''Japan Model''': Japan is an "advanced problem solving nation" that can provide social and technological solutions to global challenges.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />
* '''Three Forces of Hyper-globalization''': Explains globalization in terms of [[Hyper-globalization]] as the new environment of the 21st century being shaped by three forces of (1) massive global trade and cross-border economic integration, (2) global and instant communications of the internet, and (3) rapid disruptive technological change through advances in such things as [[big data]], [[Internet of things|Internet of Things]], and [[Artificial intelligence|Artificial Intelligence]] that is bringing massive economic and rapid social changes leading to a world of [[technological singularity]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last=Inoue|first=Dr. Takashi|date=16 October 2018|title=Hyper-Globalization and the Critical Role of PR|url=https://www.odwyerpr.com/story/public/11458/2018-10-16/hyper-globalization-critical-role-pr.html|journal=O'Dwyer's}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ipra.org/news/itle/itl-263-a-profoundly-new-environment-the-three-forces-of-hyper-globalization/|title=IPRA {{!}} ITL #263 - A profoundly new environment: the three forces of hyper-globalization|website=www.ipra.org|access-date=2019-03-11}}</ref>

== Career in public relations ==
Takashi Inoue founded Inoue Public Relations in 1970 as a Japanese PR firm focused on high technology. Between late 1970s and early 1980s he helped both Intel and Apple Inc. enter the Japan market. In 1984 he planned and executed the public relations program for the launch of the [[Apple Macintosh]] in Japan.<ref name=":1" /> In the late 1990s when Japan's trade surplus created trade friction with the U.S., his firm helped a U.S. auto parts manufacturer achieve deregulation in Japan in the Tenneco case.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Public relations in interactive age|last=Miyai|first=Yumiko|date=4 June 1997|work=The Japan Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/howtomanageyourg0000morl_l2o3/page/130|title=How to manage your global reputation : a guide to the dynamics of international public relations|last=Michael.|first=Morley|date=1998|publisher=New York University Press|isbn=0814756166|location=Washington Square, New York|pages=[https://archive.org/details/howtomanageyourg0000morl_l2o3/page/130 130]|oclc=38478552}}</ref> By bringing about changes in Japan's tax and automotive regulations in the automotive parts market, which had acted as non-tariff trade barriers, IPR helped Tenneco expand sales in Japan and helped avoided U.S. trade sanctions that U.S. President Clinton had threatened.<ref name=":3" /> These changes also resulted in Inoue Public Relations winning in 1997 the International Public Relations Association's Golden World Award Grand Prize.<ref name=":1" /> IPR also won the 2015 ([[IPRA Golden World Awards|IPRA]]) award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www2.spikes.asia/winners/2017/pr/entry.cfm?entryid=3948&award=101&order=2&direction=2|title=SUCCESSFUL DEREGULATION CAMPAIGN IN JAPAN|date=2017}}</ref> for successful deregulation public relations campaign for its client Concur Japan, Ltd.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.inoue-pr.com/eng/news/98/|title=Concur and Inoue PR Win the Double Crown: Grand Prix from Public Relations Society of Japan (PRSJ)|last=News|date=2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ipra.org/golden-world-awards/winners/|title=IPRA 2016 Grand Prix Awards: Relaxing rules on the management of expenses- Concur and Inoue Public Relations|date=2016}}</ref>

== Career in academia ==
After practicing public relations in Japan for over 30 years, he started a public relations course at Waseda University in 2004,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.inoue-pr.com/eng/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2018/05/takashi-inoue-bio-may23-2018.pdf|title=BIO|last=Inoue|first=Takashi}}</ref> which was the first of its kind at a major Japanese university. In 2009 Takashi Inoue received a Ph.D. from [[Waseda University]], as the first doctoral degree awarded for public relations, and for research for the Self-Correction Model of Public Relations. He has been teaching at the [[Kyoto University]]’s Graduate School of Management since 2012.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />
